newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken funds partnership with Harry's Farmers Market.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken funds partnership with Harry's Farmers Market.

text.p: Boston Chicken, Inc. said Friday it is funding Progressive Food Concepts, Inc., a new company that will partner with Harry's Farmers Market, Inc. to sell branded ready-to-heat prepared foods.

Saad Nadhir will resign as co-chairman and president of Boston Chicken to lead Progressive as chairman and CEO. He will work closely with Harry Blazer, chairman and CEO of Harry's, who will also serve on Progressive's board, Boston Chicken said.

Harry's owns and operates three Harry's Farmers Markets megastores and and two smaller Harry's In A Hurry stores in the Atlanta area. The company sells its own line of over 300 prepared food products and meals and over 200 proprietary bakery items.
Boston Chicken, based in Golden, Colo., franchises and operates 1,087 Boston Market stores in 38 states and Washington, D.C.
Progressive will explore, with Boston Chicken, taking a line of Boston Market prepared foods into alternate distribution channels, potentially in partnership with supermarkets.

Progressive has been funded with a $17 million loan from Boston Chicken and equity from management and private investors. Boston Chicken has the option to convert the loan into a majority stake in Progressive at a later date.
Boston Market's area developers are also expected to have a significant financial stake in the new venture.

"As the Boston Market brand has achieved national awareness through nearly 1,100 stores across the U.S., we believe it is now time to leverage the brand through complementary opportunities outside the ready-to-eat segment," said Scott Beck, chairman and CEO of Boston Chicken.
"Branded, ready-to-heat products and innovative approaches to selling fresh produce, meats and seafood appear to be sizable additional segments."
Progressive has made a $20 million loan to Harry's that can be exchanged for up to five million shares of Harry's Class A common stock and warrants for two million of the shares.
Progressive could own about 43 percent of Harry's if the company exercises all its rights to acquire Harry's stock.
The companies also have a mutual consulting agreement and Progressive will evaluate how the new company can expand Harry's retail formats outside of Georgia and Alabama.
In addition, Progressive acquired Harry's worldwide intellectual property and trademark rights, including all rights to the Harry's Farmers Market and Harry's In A Hurry retail concepts.

Harry's will retain development and trademark rights to both concepts in Georgia and Alabama and will receive a 2.5 percent equity stake in Progressive. There are no ongoing royalties or fees associated with the transfer of these rights.
Harry's will continue to own and operate all of its current stores as well as any future Harry's stores opened in Georgia and Alabama.
Boston Chicken's stock rose 21.88 cents to $36.03, while Harry's jumped $2.375 to $6.25 early on Nasdaq.
